checks.why_it_matters: Without a frozen policy on disk there is nothing to evaluate, and any policy assembled here would have been chosen after the test split existed.
The fingerprint is what lets a reader confirm that the policy evaluated here is the policy that was frozen, rather than one edited afterwards.
The frozen policy and the Phase D/E record must describe the same policy. If they disagree, one of them was edited and neither can be trusted.
Every one of these was recorded by the phase that made the decision, at the time it made it. A flag written now would prove nothing.
A sample in both pools would have contributed to the policy that is now being evaluated on it.
The pool must be the one whose fingerprint was recorded before the policy was frozen, not one re-derived now from a manifest that may have moved.

detail.pool_rule: ids present in the SAME split of both the audio and the text experiment manifest. Ids shared across DIFFERENT splits are excluded and counted, because one model trained on them.

checks.why_it_matters: The pool must contain each id once, must carry both modalities, and must not have used a label to decide membership.

selection_rule.primary_criterion: mean validation macro-F1 over the low-budget operating region ['5%', '10%', '15%', '20%', '25%'], using out-of-fold scores
selection_rule.admissibility_gate: the policy must exceed the matched-budget random control's 97.5th percentile macro-F1 at at least one interior budget
selection_rule.tie_break_1: within 0.005 macro-F1, the simpler signal wins; a fitted target must clear uncertainty_only by more than that margin to be selected over it
selection_rule.tie_break_2: higher retained fraction of the always-fusion macro-F1 gain at 10%
selection_rule.tie_break_3: alphabetical target name, so the rule is total
selection_rule.why_not_accuracy: Stage 2 measured that accuracy-shaped gating on this corpus buys neutral and loses macro-F1. Selecting on accuracy would reproduce that.
selection_rule.declared: before any Phase D estimator was fitted or scored

routing_rule.score: the frozen Stage 2/3 routing uncertainty (normalised score entropy of the Gemma response), used directly
routing_rule.decision: acquire audio on the top-k samples by score
routing_rule.tie_break: index order, so the acquired set is deterministic
routing_rule.k: budget x pool size, rounded to nearest

acquisition_budget.rule: smallest budget meeting every MATERIAL_ROUTING_SUCCESS condition

rule.A_GENERALIZES: AHSEF beats matched random acquisition on macro-F1 at the frozen budget, retains a meaningful fraction of the fusion gain, and its improvement is distributed across classes rather than confined to neutral
rule.B_PARTIAL: AHSEF offers a useful cost/performance trade-off but either does not clearly beat matched random or loses most of the fusion benefit
rule.C_DOES_NOT_GENERALIZE: AHSEF does not outperform matched random acquisition, or offers no meaningful advantage over text-only
rule.accuracy_is_not_the_criterion: Stage 2 measured that accuracy-shaped judgements on this corpus reward majority-class behaviour. Accuracy is reported beside macro-F1, never instead of it.

leakage_audit.enforced_by: the frozen policy is loaded from disk and applied; this driver has no code path that selects a target, a threshold, a budget, a weight or a model, and lock condition 4 checks the declarations every earlier phase recorded at the time it made its decisions

budget.cost_basis: provider list price per million tokens, applied to measured token counts; not an energy measurement
